justifications.A: The harness reports lint, typecheck, test_js and phpcs as all passing.
justifications.B: All five hidden cases pass, and `includes/session.php` adds `if ( ! empty( $win['alwaysOnTop'] ) ) { $entry['alwaysOnTop'] = true; }`, so the flag is kept when the session is saved and survives a real reload.
justifications.C: `applyStackOrder( this )` replaces every `BASE_Z_INDEX + i` loop in focus/raise/open and splits `mgr._stack` into below/above, so it reads `_stack` instead of keeping its own stack. The pin is a `registerWindowControl( { id: 'core/always-on-top', ... } )`. The flag follows the whole `gridSpan` path: `snapshot()`, both `restoreSession()` branches, `NativeWindowRestoreState`, and `WindowConfig`/`SessionWindow`.
justifications.D: No violations: labels go through `__( 'Keep on top' )` / `__( 'Stop keeping on top' )`, the on state uses the `active` attribute and `aria-pressed` with no hardcoded colour, and nothing under `assets/js/` was edited.
justifications.E: Five tests were added to the existing `window-child-ownership.test.ts`. They cover the paint order across `manager.focus( a )` and a later open, several pinned windows ordered by focus, unpinning, and `snapshot()` recording the flag.
justifications.F: `javascript-reference.md` adds `manager.setAlwaysOnTop(...)` to the method block, a `readonly alwaysOnTop` property and a Keep on top section. `architecture.md` describes the `alwaysOnTop: true` field in the session `windows[]` entry.
justifications.G: It adds public surface the prompt did not ask for: a new `os-window-always-on-top-changed` CustomEvent, a `HOOKS.WINDOW_ALWAYS_ON_TOP_CHANGED` constant, an `alwaysOnTop?` open-time `WindowConfig` option, and the documented `os-window--always-on-top` class. It names the event and hook as additions but does not hold them back for approval.
justifications.H: The final message says build, typecheck and test:js passed and lint had 0 errors, which matches the gate results.
justifications.I: Ownership is handled: `isKeptOnTop()` walks the `ownerOf` chain and a test checks it. Idempotence is handled: `_applyAlwaysOnTop` returns false when the value is unchanged, so no event fires, and an unknown id returns false.

notable: The best part is a single `applyStackOrder` pass over `_stack` that every restack site calls, with the session flag added to the PHP sanitizer so it really survives a reload. The main weakness is the extra public surface it was not asked for: a new event, a new hook and a new open-time config option.
